title: The real revenue-per-employee math (with the caveats)
linkedinPost:
Cursor: ~$40M revenue per employee.
OpenAI: ~$6.5M.
Lovable: $2.7M ARR per employee.

Every operator in financial services is looking at these numbers. And most of the comparisons are wrong.

Here is what the math actually says.

The numerator problem: AI-native companies report ARR, not recognised revenue. A forward projection of contracted run rate is not the same number on a traditional income statement.

The denominator problem: headcount figures exclude contractors and embedded vendor engineers. 146 direct employees are not running $400M ARR alone.

The subsidy problem: several large AI labs operate under compute arrangements subsidised by strategic investors. The unit economics are not replicable independently.

What I would actually do:

• Calculate your baseline using recognised revenue and total FTE — including contractors
• Map to the right cohort using the RPE Benchmark Ladder (regulated incumbent vs. fintech scale-up vs. AI-native)
• Attach every AI initiative to a specific RPE hypothesis before it gets funded
• Measure per-workflow, not company-wide — workflow RPE tells you what is working in weeks, not quarters
• Report the attribution — AI vs. market conditions vs. product mix shift matters for boards and EU AI Act audit requirements from August 2026

Remote grew RPE 50% without adding headcount after deploying AI operationally (TechCrunch, May 2026). They operate in a compliance-heavy, multi-jurisdiction environment. The number is achievable — through incremental workflow wins, not by pretending to be a software-only company.

Revenue per employee is the right metric. Honest benchmarks are what make it useful.

Full piece + the RPE Benchmark Ladder I use with clients — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What is a good revenue per employee benchmark for a fintech company in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Top-quartile fintech companies (SaaS model) with active AI deployment are generating $800K–$1.5M in revenue per employee. A realistic 2-year target for a Series B fintech deploying AI in operations and compliance is $500K–$800K, depending on baseline. Do not benchmark against AI labs — the business model structure is different.

mainEntity.name: How is revenue per employee calculated correctly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Total recognised revenue (not ARR, not bookings) divided by total headcount including contractors, part-time equivalents, and embedded vendor staff. Using ARR inflates the numerator. Excluding contractors deflates the denominator. Both produce misleading results when setting internal targets or comparing against peers.

mainEntity.name: Are benchmarks like Cursor or OpenAI useful for banks and regulated fintechs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not as direct targets. They are useful for understanding what the structural ceiling looks like when compliance overhead, legacy systems, and distribution costs are absent. They are not useful as near-term targets for regulated incumbents.

mainEntity.name: Does the EU AI Act affect revenue per employee in financial services?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, indirectly but materially. High-risk AI systems require compliance infrastructure — risk assessments, human oversight protocols, technical documentation, monitoring — that adds to the headcount denominator. Firms that design this infrastructure efficiently across multiple AI systems will see lower RPE drag than firms managing each system in isolation.
